title: The private tape of Louis and Zutty reminiscing
summary: Louis and Zutty made a private tape at the Alvin Hotel where he talked about Punch Miller, and Louis played Zutty's records and told his chauffeur how Zutty could push a band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Really?

Well that's something else. He tells about Punch Miller in that tape. (LAUGHTER). He let Punch Miller right on that tape. He made it himself. Lucille doesn't have that tape. Nobody has that tape. It was made in the Alvin Hotel on Louis' last go round. He and Zutty were talking about old times.
Yes. And we were talking about pictures on the wall. He said, now who is this cat? Who is this? And I would explain it to him.
I mean this tape is not a thing you would want anybody to hear, I take it? I mean you wouldn't ......
Well, we sent it to Pete (Stern ?). We let Pete tape it and I sent it to Richmond, Virginia.
It was a (unintelligible ?) tape.
Yes, a (unintelligible ?) tape.
Well I mean in other words you're not saying anything in there that you wouldn't, you'd sort of regret, really?
Oh no, no.
It was sort of joking and.....
Yes, yes.
Oh, I'd love to hear that.

Louis was telling about Punch Miller which was so.... I told Zutty it was so apropos when Punch Miller is going on and said Louis got the breaks, you know. Boy, we got the (unintelligible ?) what Louis thought about Punch Miller. How big he thought he was when he came to Chicago. You've got to hear what he says you know. It's a nice tape and he was really just reminiscing.
Yes, well that's marvellous.
They are reminiscing. And Barney and Dottie told Lucille about how they enjoyed
the tape. They played it for us and Lucille said she's got to get it, she's got to get it.
Yes, she's got to get one.
She said, yes, she's got to get one, but she doesn't know that it's just a PRIVATE tape.
Well you, it's fairly valuable.

And Louis played Zutty's records, some of his records when we were out there and he said, listen to old Zutty, how he's pushing. And he told his chauffeur that day, he said, "man," he said, "this guy sure could push a band. Yes," he said, "my man," he said, "he really plays." Oh he was bragging on Zutty like mad.
